Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Adams has opened the week with a pair of limited sessions due to a knee injury. He will have one more chance to log a full practice Friday before Arizona attempts to move to 2-0 with a win Sunday against Seattle.

Seumalo opened the week as a non-participant at the team's practice Wednesday, so his return to the field Thursday is a step in the right direction. The offensive lineman will have one more chance to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Seahawks.
Williams was limited at practice all last week before sitting out Sunday's win against the Chargers. Until he's able to practice in full, he may continue to have to miss game action.

Taylor-Demerson missed Sunday's win against the Chargers due to a rib injury, but he's making progress toward potentially playing in Week 2. He'll still probably have to log a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

It's not clear when Gibbens hurt his shoulder, but his status for Week 2 is now in question. He'll likely need to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Crawford sustained a mid ankle sprain and was carted off the field during the second half of Sunday's win against the Chargers, and now he'll have to sit out at least Arizona's next four games. Until he's able to return to action, 2024 fourth-rounder Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (ribs) and undrafted rookie Wydett Williams could be in line for a slight increase in reps.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: The offensive guard is in the concussion protocol and was not able to practice at all Wednesday, so he is making progress. Lindstrom will need to get a full session in ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Panthers to have a chance to play. If he can't go, Kyle Hinton will likely start at right guard.

Bowman passed a physical at the end of training camp, got taken off the active/PUP list and logged limited practices ahead of Week 1, but he still had to sit out of Atlanta's loss to Pittsburgh. The starting slot corner's limited participation Thursday might just be a precaution ahead of Sunday's matchup with Carolina, but if he has to miss the game, Sydney Brown should be in line to step forward in his place.

Tagovailoa officially goes down as a non-participant for a second consecutive practice. He's likely to miss a second consecutive game to begin the season Sunday against the Panthers, though Tagovailoa has one chance left to practice before then. Michael Penix (knee) would get the nod Sunday if he's cleared to suit up and Tua isn't. Otherwise, Cooper Rush would make his second start of the season.

Hand's move to injured reserve comes as no surprise since it was previously announced that he'd miss the remainder of the season due to a torn quadriceps suffered during the team's Week 1 loss to the Steelers. The 30-year-old played just seven defensive snaps and failed to log any stats before getting hurt and will now shift his focus to getting healthy for the 2027 campaign.

Penix practiced fully from Wednesday through Friday last week and ultimately was inactive for Week 1, so he is not a lock to suit up for Week 2 just yet. However -- per the same source above -- he shared the first-team work with Cooper Rush on Wednesday, and -- via Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com -- Penix himself indicated he could take the field Sunday. It likely will not be known for a day or two who will start at quarterback for the Falcons in Week 2, but at the least Penix is in the mix.

Williams was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers due to his ankle injury. The offensive tackle will evidently need more time to recover and now must miss at least four games before he is eligible to return from IR. Jake Matthews will likely get the start at left tackle in Williams' absence.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: The starting left guard also missed Wednesday's session. Simpson was able to handle all 68 offensive snaps in the Ravens' Week 1 win over the Colts, but he likely picked up the groin injury during the game. If he can't play this Sunday against the Saints, Andrew Vorhees is the next man up.

The starting left tackle also sat out of yesterday's session. Stanley played for the Ravens' entire Week 1 win over the Colts but emerged from the game with a toe injury. If he can't return to the field for this Sunday's matchup with the Saints, Carson Vinson will likely have to step in.

Hendrickson was a surprise addition to Baltimore's injury report Wednesday, and now his status for Week 2 is up in the air. He'll probably have to practice in some capacity Friday to have any chance of being active Sunday versus the Saints.

Flowers sat out Wednesday's session and did the same a day later. The speedy wide receiver will be hard-pressed to suit up Sunday if he's unable to practice in at least some capacity Friday. Fellow wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) was placed on injured reserve Wednesday, so Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker, Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester are the only healthy options in Baltimore's wide receiver room at the moment.

Madubuike was limited at practice throughout the entire week before he was ultimately unable to play during the team's 41-23 win over Indianapolis in Week 1. The defensive lineman is on the cusp of appearing in his first contest since suffering a neck injury last September, and he'll have two more opportunities to increase his participation and log a full practice before Sunday's contest against the Saints.

Buchanan was unable to play Week 1 versus the Colts after logging three limited practices, and he appears to have picked up where he left off by opening the week with another limited session. The linebacker is working his way back from a torn ACL that he suffered in Week 12 of the 2025 campaign, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with New Orleans.

Lane left the Ravens' Week 1 win at Indianapolis with a wrist injury that eventually was confirmed to include a fracture. With his move to IR, he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance for game action will come Oct. 18 at Cleveland. As long as Lane is sidelined, Zay Flowers (hamstring), Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker (groin), Elijah Sarratt and LaJohntay Wester will be among those that could see additional action at wide receiver for Baltimore.

Tampa went to the locker room late in the first quarter, and tests have revealed that his knee injury is severe enough for him to remain sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Chidobe Awuzie will be the main rotational option at outside corner behind Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins in Tampa's absence.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Head coach Joe Brady did not provide a postgame update on Moore after he left Thursday's contest in the second quarter, but more details are now available, and it appears Moore is not facing any sort of extended absence. He will have over a week to rest and recover before the Bills square off against the Chargers, and if he's unable to go by then that will mean more snaps for Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer.

Sanders was sidelined by a knee injury in Week 1 and then came down with an illness earlier in the week, and the combination of both leaves him unavailable for Week 2. In his absence, 2024 third-rounder DeWayne Carter figures to continue to see increased work on the defensive line.
Oliver injured his hip during pregame warmups and has since been ruled out. Without Oliver on the field, Landon Jackson should be in line for more snaps.

Despite being listed as limited on all three of the Bills' Week 2 injury reports, Johnson will continue to don street clothes on game days due to a hamstring issue that has bothered him since at least Aug. 24. In Johnson's absence, Ray Davis will continue to garner RB reps that don't go to starter James Cook, while Frank Gore is on hand in case one of those two leaves the game for any reason.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Brown has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week with a back injury, and he will have one more chance to practice Friday ahead of Sunday's matchup with Atlanta. The defensive lineman secured two solo tackles in the team's Week 1 loss to Chicago, and if he is unavailable Week 2, Aaron Hall and TeRah Edwards would be candidates to draw a start in Brown's place.

Jones was unavailable for the team's Week 1 loss to the Bears while nursing a back injury, but he was able to return to practice this week. The linebacker will have one more chance to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Falcons.

The Panthers continue to cap Coker's practice participation as he works through a left ankle injury that put him in a boot earlier in the week. Coker has logged a pair of limited sessions to begin the week, and Friday's session could give more clarity on his status going into Week 2. The Holy Cross product is coming off a massive outing Week 1 when he popped for 138 yards and two touchdowns. The Panthers head to Atlanta to face the Falcons on Sunday.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Monangai has been a limited participant in Chicago's first two practices heading into Sunday's battle with the NFC North rival Vikings. The second-year pro no longer seems bothered by the knee injury that forced him to miss time during the preseason, and Monangai is coming off a strong season opener in which he produced a 61-yard touchdown run. D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) also was listed as limited Thursday, so the health of Chicago's top two running backs will bear monitoring on Friday's injury report.

Swift has been limited the last two days due to a pair of lower-body injuries to his knee and ankle. Both he and Kyle Monangai (hamstring) are on the injury report, which puts the Bears' backfield outlook in question as Sunday approaches. Friday's injury report will give firmer confirmation on Swift's status going into the Week 2 divisional matchup with the Vikings.

The rookie fourth-round defensive back may have tweaked his ankle during the Bears' 59-37 win over the Panthers in Week 1, when he logged three tackles (two solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception). Muhammad will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation for the Bears' NFC North tilt against the Vikings on Sunday.

Woods popped up on the Bears' injury report last week due to a groin injury, which prevented him from playing in this past Sunday's regular-season opener against the Panthers. The Bears gave up 37 points in that game, so Woods' return against the Vikings this Sunday would be a significant boost to Chicago's secondary. The veteran safety will have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation for Week 2.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Perine was added to the injury report with an apparent knee injury after opening the week without a listed practice status Wednesday. The running back turned five carries into 20 yards and reeled in all three of his targets for 30 yards during the team's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers in Week 1, but he may have suffered a knee injury at some point during the contest. Perine will have another chance to practice Friday, but if he can't go Sunday against Houston, Tahj Brooks would stand to operate as the team's primary backup option behind Chase Brown in Cincinnati's backfield.

Burrow was limited Wednesday due to back tightness, but he was seemingly able to increase his activity level a day later. it remains to be seen whether he will ultimately go down as a limited or full participant, but Burrow looks poised to suit up this weekend, barring a setback.

Taylor signed a one-year contract with the Bengals in early April. The cornerback is set to play a key reserve role in the team's secondary once he can return to the field. Taylor will need to miss at least the first four games of the regular season on IR before becoming eligible to return to the Bengals' active roster.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: The starting center was limited Wednesday as well. If the issue is serious enough to keep Jenkins out of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Parker Brailsford (thumb) and Luke Wypler are in line to step in.
The offensive guard was not able to play in Week 1 due to the back issue. At the moment, he's not on track to play in Week 2, either. Austin Barber has been his replacement at right guard.

Campbell was a new addition to the injury report Thursday, so it appears he might have suffered an ankle injury during Wednesday's practice. He'll likely have to practice in some capacity Friday to have an opportunity to play in Week 2.

It's unclear exactly how much time Sampson will miss. He is expected back this season, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer, but his placement on IR means he will miss at least the next four games. Jaleel McLaughlin was brought up from the practice squad, and both he and Raheim Sanders -- who played 18 snaps on offense and got four touches Sunday after Sampson's exit -- will work behind starter Quinshon Judkins.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Overshown is expected to miss one to two weeks with the hamstring injury he suffered during Sunday's loss against the Giants, so his absence from practice Wednesday makes sense. He'd probably need to return to practice Thursday or Friday to give himself a chance to suit up in Week 2.

Hooker fractured his forearm during Sunday's loss against the Giants, so it's not a big surprise he was unable to practice Wednesday. It seems likely at this point he'll be unavailable come Sunday versus the Commanders.

Davis underwent surgery Saturday for a hip injury, and Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports that the procedure will sideline the 27-year-old running back for the entire 2026 season. With Davis on the shelf, the Cowboys bolstered their backfield depth by signing Israel Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster, with the latter serving as the RB3 behind Javonte Williams and Emari Demercado.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Mims has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week while dealing with a foot injury. The wide receiver will have one more chance to practice Friday before the team hosts Jacksonville on Sunday. If Mims can't go against the Jaguars, it would carry the largest impact on special teams for Denver.

Harvey was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's practice estimate, but he's set to participate in at least some capacity now that Denver's actually holding practice Thursday. The 2025 second-round pick turned seven touches into 41 yards from scrimmage in Monday's loss to the Chiefs and got all four targets among Denver's running backs while J.K. Dobbins took most of the rushing work. Harvey's availability bears monitoring ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Jaguars.

Cooper now has a jury trial scheduled to begin Nov. 10 following a pair of domestic incidents that occurred a week apart in early June. The NFL placed him on the Commissioner's Exempt List on Sunday, which means he still gets paid and can attend team meetings but can't practice or play in games. Cooper's stint on the list is indefinite but may last for as long as his legal situation is playing out in court.

The offensive guard began camp on the active/PUP list and was never activated, prompting the move to reserve/PUP for the start of the regular season. Now, Gargiulo will have to miss at least the first four games of the 2026 campaign. The 2024 seventh-round pick should play a backup role once he's able to return.

The offensive tackle can return for Denver's Week 5 matchup with the Chargers at the earliest. Crum suffered a leg injury during the Broncos' second preseason against the Packers and missed the last week of training camp. The third-year pro projects as a depth tackle even when healthy.

Lohner underwent a procedure in June to address a lower-body injury, and he remained sidelined throughout the preseason. The tight end will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the 2026 regular season, and the earliest he could make his season debut is in Week 5 against the Chargers on Oct. 11.

Bailey will now spend the entirety of the 2026 campaign on injured reserve unless he is waived with an injury settlement. The linebacker sustained a broken leg in last Friday's preseason opener, so he will likely remain on the team's injured reserve for the season instead of settling.

Detroit Lions.longComment: It's not looking good for the safety/cornerback, who had to leave Thursday's 41-31 loss to the Bills during the first half. Maddox had started the first two games at strong safety for Detroit with Brian Branch (Achilles) beginning the season on the reserve/PUP list. It appears now that the Lions may have to turn to Thomas Harper to man the position.
Miller is dealing with an apparent knee injury, and he will be forced to sit out Week 2. In his absence, Larry Borom will likely draw the start at right tackle versus the Bills.

Mahogany suffered a hip injury Week 1 against the Saints, and he will now be forced to miss at least one contest as a result. In his absence, Miles Frazier will operate as the top reserve option behind Ben Bartch and Tate Ratledge at offensive guard in Buffalo.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: The starting left guard was limited Wednesday as well after missing Green Bay's Week 1 loss to Minnesota. Banks was also unable to fully practice ahead of that contest. Donovan Jennings is Green Bay's first backup guard in case Banks can't go this Sunday against the Jets.
The starting right tackle was also limited Wednesday. He played through the knee injury in Week 1 but appears to still be dealing with the issue. Bako-Bewele was also limited in practice last week.

The defensive tackle was limited Wednesday. Hargrave played on 29 defensive snaps and one special-teams snap last week against Minnesota, making one tackle. If he can't go Sunday, Jonathan Ford is the next man up at nose tackle.

Wyatt was able to play 53 percent of the team's defensive snaps while recording three solo tackles in Green Bay's 39-22 loss to the Vikings in Week 1 after he was limited at practice the entire week. The defensive lineman appears to be on the same track ahead of Week 2, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Jets.

Van Ness recorded four solo tackles, including 1.0 sacks, in the team's 39-22 loss to the Vikings in Week 1, but he appears to have suffered a concussion at some point in the contest. The 25-year-old's ability to practice in any capacity is a positive sign, but he will have to clear concussion protocol in order to play Sunday on the road versus the Jets.

Houston Texans.longComment: Head coach DeMeco Ryans stated Clowney would practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session. However, that wasn't the case. The 33-year-old has battled multiple injuries of late, but it didn't stop him from suiting up for Sunday's 36-31 loss to Buffalo in Week 1. Clowney will have another opportunity to practice Friday.

Collins injured his hamstring at Wednesday's practice, and although he was listed as limited on Houston's first practice report of the week, he was tagged as a 'DNP' a day later. He's believed to be dealing with a Grade 1 strain and reportedly is not facing an extended absence, but his availability for Week 2 will likely hinge on whether or not he can get any work in at Friday's session.

To'oTo'o landed on injured reserve Tuesday, which will keep him off the field for at least four games. However, according to Garafolo, the 25-year-old is expected to be out "longer," possibly missing up to eight weeks. To'oTo'o finished the 2025 campaign by amassing 95 total tackles and 2.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games.

Hummel suffered a groin injury in the third quarter of Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills. The linebacker will almost certainly miss the Texans' Week 2 game against the Bengals. Jake Hansen will likely start as the second outside linebacker in Hummel's absence, but the team will probably rely on more nickel packages with Jalen Pitre in the slot while Hummel is absent.

McDonald was limited in practice Wednesday and missed practice Thursday, suggesting he suffered the injury in practice this week. He'll now be required to miss at least the first four games of the season. Logan Hall, Mario Edwards and Jaden Crumedy will see the rotational snaps at defensive tackle behind Tommy Togiai and Sheldon Rankins.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Giddens was a healthy scratch in Week 1, so it seems he may have hurt his knee during practice Wednesday. He'll probably have to return to practice Friday to give himself a chance at suiting up Sunday at Kansas City.

Dulin missed a second consecutive practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. The 29-year-old wideout was held without a catch in Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens. He also saw action as a member of special teams, as expected. If Dulin can't suit up for the Week 2 meeting with the Chiefs, Seth McGowan may be even busier returning kicks.

Pierce was a full participant at Wednesday's session but was unable to take the practice field Thursday. The banged-up wide receiver played through his heel injury in the Week 1 loss to Baltimore, during which he also sustained a wrist issue. The latter concern doesn't seem to be bothering him any longer, but Pierce likely will need to upgrade back to full participation Friday to avoid being listed with a designation for Sunday night's game against the Chiefs.

Montgomery signed with the team in early August, ultimately reeling in two of three targets for 21 yards during the preseason. The wide receiver appears to have picked up an abdominal injury at some point during the preseason, and he is now set to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he reaches an injury settlement with Indianapolis.

Mallory suffered a thumb injury, and he sat out the team's last two games of the preseason. The tight end will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the 2026 campaign, and the earliest he'll be able to make his regular-season debut is in Week 5 against the Steelers on Oct. 11.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Van Lanen was limited for a second straight day to open the week as he continues to nurse a knee injury. The offensive lineman was limited throughout the entire week before playing in the team's Week 1 win over the Browns, and he appears to be on a similar track prior to Sunday's matchup with Denver.

It's still unknown exactly when Oluokun picked up the wrist issue, but his availability for Week 2 now seems to be in jeopardy regardless. He'll likely need to practice in full Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Meyers emerged from preseason Week 2 with a brace on his right hand, but the nature of the injury wasn't confirmed until the Jaguars posted their first injury report of the season last week. Since then, he's been listed as limited on all five of the team's practice reports with a thumb injury, but it didn't stop him from suiting up for this past Sunday's season-opening win against the Browns, when he hauled in both targets for 40 yards and one touchdown and recorded one carry for two yards on a 65 percent snap share. If Meyers follows last week's trajectory this week, he'll enter the weekend without a designation for Sunday's contest at Denver.

Thomas now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt due to a shoulder injury to kick off Week 2 prep, which isn't unexpected after coach Liam Coen told Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com on Monday that the wide receiver would be limited in practice this week. Nevertheless, Thomas now has one more chance to get back to full Friday before the jaguars potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game at Denver.

Green sustained the injury while on punt coverage during the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns in Week 1. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve, meaning he'll be forced to miss at least the next four games. The earliest Green is eligible to return from IR is Week 6 against the Texans on Sunday, Oct. 18.

Allen played one offensive snap in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns last Sunday, suggesting he doesn't have much of a role on offense behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez. Allen can be ignored in redraft fantasy leagues.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: McDonald will now be forced to miss at least four games after sustaining a knee injury during Monday's win over the Broncos. Ashton Gillotte, R Mason Thomas and Jack Pyburn should be in line for increased playing time in McDonald's absence.

Jones was able to play through the tension in his calf in Monday's win versus the Broncos, so it's unlikely his availability for Week 2 is in any true jeopardy. A full practice Thursday or Friday would clear up any lingering doubt going into the weekend.

Norman-Lott was placed on the active/PUP list ahead of training camp, and he did not appear in a preseason game as he continues to recover from a torn ACL that he suffered in October. The defensive lineman will now be forced to miss at least four contests to begin the regular season, and in his absence, rookie first-rounder Peter Woods will handle the primary reserve role at defensive tackle behind Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

Holiday is dealing with an undisclosed injury, and he did not play during the preseason. The wide receiver will now be forced to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he is able to reach an injury settlement with Kansas City.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Since undergoing a meniscus trim in his left knee on Tuesday, Sept. 8, Bowers hasn't been able to practice in any capacity and sat out a Week 1 win against the Dolphins. He thus has just one more chance to mix into drills Friday before the Raiders potentially make a ruling on his status for Sunday's game at the Chargers. If Bowers ultimately can't go this weekend, Michael Mayer will be the primary beneficiary at tight end for Las Vegas.

Porter was deemed questionable late in the game and didn't return. He logged two tackles and two defensed passes in the season-opening win. Porter will presumably be examined by the team's training staff before his availability for practice next week is determined.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: McConkey was spotted working with the training staff during the media-viewing portion of Thursday's session, and he wound up not getting any work in for the second time in as many days. Head coach Jim Harbaugh tagged McConkey day-to-day earlier this week, but the wide receiver will be hard-pressed to take the field Sunday against the Raiders if he sits out again Friday.

Molden tweaked his hamstring during the Chargers' 26-14 loss to the Cardinals this past Sunday, finishing the game with five tackles (three solo). He'll have two more chances to return to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of the Chargers' Week 2 tilt against the Raiders this Sunday. Rookie fourth-rounder Genesis Smith and veteran Tony Jefferson would be the top candidates to start at safety alongside Derwin James if Molden is not cleared to play against Las Vegas.

Lambert-Smith suffered a significant hamstring injury during the Chargers' Week 1 loss against the Cardinals, warranting a stint on the IR. As such, the second-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games and is eligible to return for Week 6 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Oct. 18, though he may need more time to recover. Gary Jennings was signed to the Chargers' 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Speights came away from the Rams' loss against the 49ers in Week 1 with a hip pointer, but he was able to play through it and finish that contest. He has two more opportunities to log a full practice before the Rams release their last injury report of the week Saturday.

The expectation earlier in the week was that Landman was on track to play in Week 2 versus the Giants, and a limited practice Thursday keeps that door open. He'll have two more chances to practice in full before the Rams publish their final injury report of the week Saturday.

Kinchens sustained a hamstring injury during the Rams' loss against the 49ers in Week 1, and he's still working through that as the club starts to prepare for Week 2. He'll likely have to return to practice Friday or Saturday to give himself a shot to suit up Monday versus the Giants.

Curl came away from the Rams' loss in Week 1 with ankle soreness, and he's still dealing with that as the team begins a new week of preparation. He'll have two opportunities to upgrade to a full practice before the Rams' last injury report of the week is released Saturday.

This is a procedural move as Rams coach Sean McVay already announced earlier in the week that Garrett would go on IR following his knee scope. The Rams will be without their biggest offseason acquisition for at least the next four contests, leaving his earliest return date Week 6 when they host the Cardinals.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Robinson went backwards with his participation after logging a limited session to open the week Wednesday. The defensive lineman is dealing with a concussion, and he appears to be unlikely to be available Sunday versus the 49ers. If he is unable to play, Malik Herring and Robert Beal would both be candidates to draw a start in Robinson's place on the defensive line.

Louis is set to miss a few weeks due to the knee injury he suffered in last Sunday's 27-13 loss to the Raiders. The Dolphins' defensive back will need to miss at least four games before he can return from IR. With Louis sidelined, Dante Trader is set to be the starting strong safety for the team.

It's unclear whether the injury is to the same hamstring that limited Harrison's practice participation this past week. He did not log a tackle prior to his exit, and Jackson Woodard is the remaining depth option at linebacker for as long as Harrison is out of the game.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: The starting right tackle was a limited participant a day earlier. O'Neill played on all 65 offensive snaps in Week 1 against Green Bay but emerged from the contest with a knee injury. Now he's trending in the wrong direction as Week 2 approaches.

Murray lasted only 11 offensive snaps before suffering a concussion during this past Sunday's 39-22 win against the Packers. It's generally a positive sign that he's been able to log some on-field activity in both Week 2 practices to date, but he likely will need to bump up to full participation Friday to give himself a chance to play Sunday in Chicago. If Murray isn't able to gain clearance from an independent neurologist ahead of that contest, Carson Wentz will direct the Vikings offense this weekend.

The Vikings' starting weakside linebacker logged 1.5 sacks over 55 defensive snaps in last Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers. While Van Ginkel had a strong showing, the linebacker likely suffered his chest injury during the game. The 31-year-old will need to upgrade to full practice participation by Friday to avoid an injury designation ahead of next Sunday's game against the Bears.

New England Patriots.longComment: Davis missed just one defensive snap of the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks last Wednesday, playing the other 49 and logging three tackles (two solo). The cornerback is dealing with a neck injury, and if he cannot upgrade to at least limited practice participation by Thursday, he will likely miss next Sunday's game against the Steelers.

The Patriots deactivated Brown just three days after he sustained the injury in the third quarter of Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks. Though recovery timelines for high-ankle sprains often range from 4-to-6 weeks, the Patriots quickly determined that Brown's injury is "a little more serious," which likely takes a return from IR in Week 6 when first eligible off the table. While their No. 1 wideout is sidelined until early November, the Patriots will have to lean more heavily on Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins and Kyle Williams as their primary receivers.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Per Terrell, the injury is significant enough to potentially keep Wood sidelined for 4-to-6 weeks. The Saints are currently without a healthy long-snapper on their 53-man roster, but defensive tackle John Ridgeway was their emergency long-snapper during training camp.

The edge rusher did not have an injury designation a day earlier. Young also played on 59 defensive snaps and broke up a pass in the Saints' Week 1 loss the Lions. His status for Week 2 is now a little bit in doubt.

The defensive end missed the Saints' Week 1 loss to the Lions and was limited in practice Wednesday as well. Jordan has been dealing with the hamstring issue since early August, but he is at least trending in the right direction ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

The tight end has been dealing with the hamstring issue since August and had to miss the Saints' Week 1 loss to the Lions. Delp had to miss practices last week, though, so he is at least trending in the right direction. The third-round pick in April's draft is still trying to make his regular-season NFL debut.

Johnson took a step in the right direction after sitting out practice entirely Wednesday. He still has a chance to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens if Johnson can upgrade to full participation Friday. Johnson caught three of seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints' Week 1 overtime loss at Detroit.

Olave showed up on the Saints' second Week 2 practice report Thursday with a hamstring injury, which may stem from the cramping that he dealt with Week 1 during a 10-182-0 performance on 13 targets at Detroit. Friday's injury report will reveal whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game in Baltimore, but his status may not be entirely confirmed until about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

Estime was ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit with a thigh injury. The running back's injury came out of nowhere but movement to IR likely means it is a significant issue. Estime will need to miss the first four games of the regular season before he is eligible to return to the field.

New York Giants.longComment: The exact nature of his injury is still unknown, but Newsome's status for Week 2 is now up in the air. If he can't return to practice in full Friday, he might end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News, Banks was working off to the side with trainers Thursday. It's not clear when he sustained the calf injury, but it doesn't look like it's anything too severe. If he's able to manage a full practice Friday, he could still avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

New York Jets.longComment: Ossai sat out Sunday's win at Tennessee due to a foot injury he suffered during the preseason, and he still hasn't been able to return to practice. Unless he can practice in some capacity Friday, he'll likely be sidelined again in Week 2 versus the Packers.

McDonald was a new addition to the Jets' injury report Thursday, so it looks like he might have gotten hurt during practice Wednesday. He'll probably need to practice in full Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Cooper's inability to practice is no surprise considering he's expected to miss multiple weeks due to an ankle sprain he sustained in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans. Prior to getting hurt in the first quarter of his NFL debut, the rookie first-round pick had a 30-yard catch and run. Expect Cooper to be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers when the Jets release game statuses Friday.

Fitzpatrick left Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans due to a groin injury. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz on Tuesday, the veteran safety is expected to miss two to three weeks, so he's unlikely to play against the Packers on Sunday unless he manages to practice in at least a limited capacity this week. Andre Cisco figures to start alongside Dane Belton at safety for as long as Fitzpatrick is sidelined.

The 2021 fourth-rounder is considered week-to-week due to a back injury, so his absence from Wednesday's practice isn't a surprise. Nwangwu will have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity, which would give him a chance to return for Sunday's home game against the Packers.

Patrick was ruled out ahead of Sunday's contest after Friday's practice. The wide receiver's groin injury seems to be lingering, so the 32-year-old will spend some time on IR. Patrick will be eligible to return from IR after four games, meaning Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith will likely see a greater share of reserve opportunities with the Jets' wide receiver corps.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Per Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer, Mukuba was wearing a sleeve on his left leg Thursday, but he told reporters he was okay. The picture should at least be a bit clearer when the Eagles publish their last injury report of the week Friday.

Per Eliot Shorr-Parks of Sports Radio 94 WIP Philadelphia, Carter said Thursday, "I'm playing this week." His lack of full participation at practice leaves a bit of space for skepticism, but that could get cleared up when the Eagles release their final injury report of the week Friday.

Per Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia, Greenard said Thursday that he was close to being available for game action again, but he's still not sure whether that will be the case in Week 2. His status on the Eagles' official injury report Friday may provide some clarity on that front.

Dejean missed practice with a calf issue Wednesday, but he was able to get back onto the practice field Thursday. If he can upgrade to full participation Friday, he could still avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

Dickerson injured his knee in the Eagles' 24-22 win over the Commanders last Sunday. The left guard will now need to miss at least four games before he can return to the active roster from IR. Willie Lampkin is set to be the starting left guard while Dickerson recovers.

Stowers has been dealing with a hamstring injury since at least Aug. 24, which limited him in all three Week 1 practices before the Eagles tabbed him as questionable for Sunday's season opener against the Commanders. At the same time the team placed him on IR, he was ruled out with not only the hamstring issue but a quad concern. The rookie second-round pick thus will miss at least the first four games of the campaign, allowing Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins to handle the TE reps that don't go to No. 1 option Dallas Goedert.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Porter's back injury was added to his designation after it appeared that he was past the issue a day earlier, when he was listed as limited due to conditioning. The cornerback expressed dissatisfaction during training camp because he didn't get a contract extension from the team. There's a lot going on with Porter, and if he can't play Sunday, Asante Samuel should again be in line to step in.

Pittman took a step in the wrong direction Thursday after being listed as a limited participant Wednesday. The starting wide receiver's participation level during Friday's practice and subsequent injury status on Friday's injury report will bear monitoring as the Steelers prepare for Sunday's matchup with the Patriots.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Pineiro has missed consecutive practices to open the week as he battles an illness, and his status for Sunday's matchup against Miami remains in question. The 31-year-old will have one more chance to practice Friday. If he can't go this week, San Francisco will have to sign a free agent to handle the team's starting kicker role for Week 2.

Black did not show up on Wednesday's injury report, but he was unable to get a full session in a day later. The extent of his injury is uncertain, but his status will be updated again Friday when the 49ers release their final report before Sunday's matchup with the Dolphins.

Kittle continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps in the early going this season, which isn't a surprise considering he tore his right Achilles nine months ago. In Week 1 against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, he recorded two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards on a 46 percent snap share, more or less looking like his normal self. Because WRs De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee) and Christian Kirk (calf) are all sidelined for varying lengths of time, Kittle stands to benefit in the 49ers' passing game, assuming he's active on a weekly basis.

The team placed Tonges on injured reserve earlier Wednesday, and now it's official that he will miss the rest of the season. Tonges suffered an MCL tear in the season opener against the Rams. Jack Stoll was signed to the practice squad to add depth, and Luke Farrell now projects to be the second tight end behind George Kittle.

Stribling wasn't able to return to the 49ers' Week 1 win against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, after appearing to pick up a non-contact injury to his lower left leg. He eventually was diagnosed with an ankle injury after his Achilles was shown to be intact, but he'll need some time on the sideline. Once he's on IR, Stribling will be required to miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance for game action would be Monday, Oct. 19, versus the Commanders.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: The guard was limited Wednesday as well and is also now dealing with a hip injury, per Smith. Christian Haynes is Bradford's backup.

The slot cornerback didn't play in the Seahawks' Week 1 win over the Patriots after practicing on a limited basis ahead of that contest as well. He is looking likely to at least enter the weekend with an injury designation. Emmanwori enjoyed a standout rookie campaign a year ago, recording 81 tackles (56 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and 11 pass breakups, including an interception, during the regular season.
The safety missed his fifth straight practice session to open the regular season and also didn't play in Week 1 against the Patriots. Okada does not appear ready to return for Week 2, either.

Darnold lasted just five plays into the Seahawks' Super Bowl defense before leaving last Wednesday's Week 1 matchup with the Patriots due to what was initially described as a hip injury. After a series of updates since then, Darnold is believed to be tending to a "very unique" glute injury that is accompanied by a recovery timetable of four weeks, per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock will direct Seattle's offense.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: The safety was also limited Wednesday. Killebrew will need to practice in full ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Browns to have a chance to play. The veteran played on 15 special-teams snaps and two defensive snaps in Week 1 against the Bengals, making one tackle.

Parrish sustained a back sprain during Sunday's loss at Cincinnati, but his presence at practice Wednesday signals it's not anything too severe. He could avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend by managing a full practice Thursday or Friday.

Kamara suffered a sprained left knee in the Buccaneers' preseason finale against the Jaguars last Friday. The linebacker was promptly waived with an injury designation and cleared waivers. Kamara will now spend the entirety of the 2026 regular season on IR unless he is waived with an injury settlement.

Sills appears to have picked up an undisclosed injury at some point during the preseason. The wide receiver played in one of the team's preseason contests, reeling in one of two targets for minus-1 yard. Sills will now be forced to miss at least four contests while on IR, and the earliest he can return to action is Week 5 against the Cowboys on Oct. 8.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Gray is working his way back from a concussion he suffered on Sept. 7 during a UTV accident, and it seems he's close to clearing the league's five-step concussion protocol. If he receives clearance for game action from a neurologist in the next couple days, he should be available Sunday versus the Eagles.

It's currently unclear what issue Brooks is dealing with, but he was waived/injured Sunday and subsequently cleared waivers. As such, he's been placed on season-ending IR. Brooks could still play in 2026, though, if he works out an injury settlement with the Titans.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Lane was an unexpected addition to the Commanders' injury report Wednesday, and now his status for Week 2 genuinely appears to be in question. Unless he logs a full practice Friday, there's a decent chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Okonkwo has missed Washington's first two practices ahead of a Week 2 clash with the NFC East rival Cowboys. The offseason acquisition was injured in his Commanders debut against the Eagles. John Bates would take on an expanded role if Okonkwo sits out Sunday against Dallas, with more snaps likely available for Ben Sinnott as well.

Magee suffered a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter of the Commanders' 24-22 loss to the Eagles on Sunday. His placement on IR means Magee will be forced to miss at least the next four games, making Week 6 against the 49ers on Monday, Oct. 19 the earliest he can return. Frankie Luvu (groin) also sustained an injury against Philadelphia, and if cannot play against the Cowboys in Week 2, then Leo Chenal would likely fill in as the Commanders' second starting inside linebacker alongside rookie first-rounder Sonny Styles.

Armstrong was reinstated after serving a one-game suspension Monday, but he now appears to be dealing with a potential knee issue as practice gets underway ahead of Week 2. The linebacker will have two more chances to log a full practice and erase any doubt about his availability for Sunday's matchup with Dallas.

Oweh was limited throughout the team's entire week of practice prior to playing 46 snaps on defense in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Eagles. The linebacker will have two more chances to log a full practice before Washington's matchup with Dallas in Week 2, but he seems likely to be active again.

Luvu suffered a groin injury in the team's 24-22 loss to the Eagles in Week 1, and as result, he was unable to give it a go at Washington's first practice of the week. The linebacker will have two more chances to return to the practice field prior to Sunday's contest in Dallas.
